Checking feature flags and role settings to understand how the sidebar is tailored.

Found a double rate-limiting bug in login. The auth-service uses a 26-zero sentinel org while the login action uses an empty string org. Both consume the same "auth:login" bucket, which is not in RATE_LIMIT_BUCKETS, so the request hits the default rate limit independently twice.

The session cookie is named taskflow_session. It is httpOnly, sameSite lax, and secure in production. The raw base64url token is never stored; only its SHA256 hash is kept in the database. Passwords are stored as scrypt hashes and never returned to the client. The SessionPrincipal action result includes userId, email, activeOrgId, and expiresAt. RememberMe is validated but unused, so the session always lasts 30 days.

The proxy layer only checks for the session cookie and redirects missing cookies to /login. The dashboard layout performs the actual signed-in check via getSessionPrincipal, redirecting to /login if null. That function resolves the cookie hash, validates expiry against parseIso versus Date.now(), and returns null for expired sessions. The login page redirects authenticated users to /orgs or the next parameter. A GET /api/auth/session endpoint exposes the principal for client-side rechecks.

The /orgs page redirects to the single organization slug when a user has exactly one org. In the organization layout, getSessionPrincipal resolves the actor by finding the member record with status "active". It builds an Actor object and asserts org scope twice. It updates last seen and snapshots feature flags into client context via OrgProvider. The sidebar and navigation then filter items using visibleNav, which checks permissions and flag states.

The `can()` permission check follows four layers: matching orgId, platform staff bypass, ROLE_MATRIX rank, and ownership escalations.

Sidebar navigation is gated by role and feature flags. Overview, projects, issues, inbox, and members are readable by viewers or higher. Activity feed requires member+ plus the `activity_feed` flag. Billing settings require owner. Flag management requires admin plus the `flags` flag. Webhook management requires admin plus the `webhooks` flag. Export requires admin plus the `export` flag.

The new project button requires member+ permissions. Feature flags can also hide navigation items based on plan or role.

Later mutations flow through withAction into getActor, then getSessionPrincipal, resolveActorForOrg, and finally assertCan inside the handler.

The login page uses safeDestination to prevent open redirects.

Email lookup normalizes input to lowercase via toLowerCase in findUserByEmail. The login schema should be checked for similar lowercasing.

Password verification runs scrypt with NFKC normalization, uses timingSafeEqual, and returns false for malformed hashes.

content.text:
Signing in starts in the login form, ends as an `Actor` scoped to one organization, and the sidebar is whatever `can()` allows that actor to see.

## The form

`LoginForm` in `src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx` is a client component. On submit it reads the email, password, and “Keep me signed in” checkbox, and parses them with `loginSchema` from `src/schemas/auth.ts`. The email is lowercased and capped at 254 characters (`emailSchema` in `src/schemas/common.ts`). The password only has to be non-empty. A failed parse returns field errors and never calls the server. A successful parse calls the server action `loginAction` in `src/actions/auth/login.ts`.

The login page (`src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`) has already decided where a success should go. It reads `?next=`, keeps only a same-site path (`safeDestination` rejects anything that does not start with a single `/`), and otherwise uses `/orgs`. If `getSessionPrincipal()` already returns someone, the page redirects there and the form is never shown.

## Checking the credentials

`loginAction` parses `loginSchema` again. Then, still before any user lookup:

1. `consumeRateLimit(ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID, "auth:login")` in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`. `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID` (an empty string, from `src/actions/_lib/permission-resources.ts`) is the bucket used because there is no tenant yet. `"auth:login"` is not a named bucket, so the default capacity of 30 applies. A denial throws `RateLimitedError`.
2. `login(parsed.data)` in `src/server/services/auth-service.ts` charges the same bucket a second time, this time against the sentinel org id `"00000000000000000000000000"`. Another denial throws “Too many sign-in attempts; try again shortly”.

Only then does `login` look anyone up:

3. `userRepo.findUserByEmail` (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`) selects from the global `users` table by lowercased email. `toUser` in `src/server/repositories/_mappers.ts` maps the row onto the `User` type and leaves `password_hash` behind. An unknown email throws “Those credentials did not match”.
4. `userRepo.findPasswordHash` reads `users.password_hash` through a separate accessor so the hash never rides on `User`.
5. `verifyPassword` in `src/lib/hash.ts` splits the stored `scrypt:<saltHex>:<keyHex>` string, derives a key with `scrypt` over the NFKC-normalized password, and compares with `timingSafeEqual`. A missing hash, a malformed hash, or a mismatch all throw the same “Those credentials did not match”.

The password is not stored, logged, or returned. `rememberMe` is validated and then ignored; nothing in `loginAction` or `login` reads it.

## What is created, what is stored, what the browser receives

On a match, `login` calls `createSessionToken(user.id)` in `src/server/services/session-service.ts`:

- `randomToken(32)` (`src/lib/hash.ts`) produces 32 random bytes as a base64url string. That raw token is the secret.
- `hashToken` is SHA-256 of that string. `sessionRepo.createSession` (`src/server/repositories/session-repository.ts`) inserts one row into `sessions` (`src/server/db/schema/users.ts`): a new id, `userId`, `activeOrgId: null`, the token hash, `createdAt` / `updatedAt`, and `expiresAt` thirty days out (`SESSION_TTL_DAYS`). The raw token is not written. A dump of `sessions` cannot be replayed as a login.
- The function returns `{ token, expiresAt }`. `login` returns `{ user, token }` to the action. The action discards `user`.

`loginAction` then calls `resolveSession(token)`, which hashes the token again and loads the row through `findSessionByTokenHash`. That returns a `SessionPrincipal`: `userId`, `email`, `activeOrgId` (null on a fresh login), and `expiresAt`. There is no session id and no token on that type. If the lookup misses, the action throws `UnauthorizedActionError`.

`setSessionCookie` in `src/lib/session.ts` is the only writer of the cookie jar. It sets `taskflow_session` (`SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` in `src/schemas/session.ts`) to the raw token, `httpOnly`, `sameSite: "lax"`, `secure` in production, `path: "/"`, expiring at `principal.expiresAt`.

The action result sent back to the form is `{ ok: true, data: principal }`. So the browser’s JavaScript sees the user id, email, active org (null), and expiry. The password stays in `users.password_hash`. The token hash stays in `sessions.token_hash`. The raw token exists only inside the `Set-Cookie` header.

`LoginForm`’s effect then calls `router.push(next)`.

## The next request, and “still signed in”

2. No cookie returns null.

## From a user id to an actor the workspace can authorize

## Why the sidebar matches the role

`AppSidebar` (`src/components/domain/nav/app-sidebar.tsx`) does not branch on `actor.role`. It calls `visibleNav(SIDEBAR_NAV, actor, flags)` and `visibleNav(SETTINGS_NAV, actor, flags)` from `src/config/nav.ts`. Each `NavItem` names a `PermissionAction` and sometimes a feature flag. `visibleNav` drops an item when its flag is off, or when `can(actor, action, navResource(action, actor))` is false, and it drops a parent left with no children.

`can` / `explain` in `src/lib/permissions.ts` decide in this order: the actor’s `orgId` must equal the resource’s `orgId`; platform staff bypass; otherwise `ROLE_RANK` (`src/types/member.ts`: owner 4, admin 3, member 2, viewer 1) is compared with `ROLE_MATRIX`. Ownership can escalate a few content actions; nav checks are org-wide, so they stop at the role. A viewer still gets Overview, Projects, Issues, Inbox, and Members (`*:read` is `viewer`). Activity requires `member`. Billing requires `owner`. Feature flags and webhooks require `admin`. Export requires `admin`. `DashboardShell` adds “New project” only when `can(actor, "project:create", …)` passes, which is `member` and above. Flags such as `activity_feed`, `kanban_board`, and `advanced_search` hide entries by plan even when the role would allow them. The settings sub-nav in `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/layout.tsx` runs the same `can()` filter on its own tab list, so a member who cannot manage billing never sees that tab.

result:
Signing in starts in the login form, ends as an `Actor` scoped to one organization, and the sidebar is whatever `can()` allows that actor to see.

## The form

`LoginForm` in `src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx` is a client component. On submit it reads the email, password, and “Keep me signed in” checkbox, and parses them with `loginSchema` from `src/schemas/auth.ts`. The email is lowercased and capped at 254 characters (`emailSchema` in `src/schemas/common.ts`). The password only has to be non-empty. A failed parse returns field errors and never calls the server. A successful parse calls the server action `loginAction` in `src/actions/auth/login.ts`.

The login page (`src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`) has already decided where a success should go. It reads `?next=`, keeps only a same-site path (`safeDestination` rejects anything that does not start with a single `/`), and otherwise uses `/orgs`. If `getSessionPrincipal()` already returns someone, the page redirects there and the form is never shown.

## Checking the credentials

`loginAction` parses `loginSchema` again. Then, still before any user lookup:

1. `consumeRateLimit(ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID, "auth:login")` in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`. `ANONYMOUS_ORG_ID` (an empty string, from `src/actions/_lib/permission-resources.ts`) is the bucket used because there is no tenant yet. `"auth:login"` is not a named bucket, so the default capacity of 30 applies. A denial throws `RateLimitedError`.
2. `login(parsed.data)` in `src/server/services/auth-service.ts` charges the same bucket a second time, this time against the sentinel org id `"00000000000000000000000000"`. Another denial throws “Too many sign-in attempts; try again shortly”.

Only then does `login` look anyone up:

3. `userRepo.findUserByEmail` (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`) selects from the global `users` table by lowercased email. `toUser` in `src/server/repositories/_mappers.ts` maps the row onto the `User` type and leaves `password_hash` behind. An unknown email throws “Those credentials did not match”.
4. `userRepo.findPasswordHash` reads `users.password_hash` through a separate accessor so the hash never rides on `User`.
5. `verifyPassword` in `src/lib/hash.ts` splits the stored `scrypt:<saltHex>:<keyHex>` string, derives a key with `scrypt` over the NFKC-normalized password, and compares with `timingSafeEqual`. A missing hash, a malformed hash, or a mismatch all throw the same “Those credentials did not match”.

The password is not stored, logged, or returned. `rememberMe` is validated and then ignored; nothing in `loginAction` or `login` reads it.

## What is created, what is stored, what the browser receives

On a match, `login` calls `createSessionToken(user.id)` in `src/server/services/session-service.ts`:

- `randomToken(32)` (`src/lib/hash.ts`) produces 32 random bytes as a base64url string. That raw token is the secret.
- `hashToken` is SHA-256 of that string. `sessionRepo.createSession` (`src/server/repositories/session-repository.ts`) inserts one row into `sessions` (`src/server/db/schema/users.ts`): a new id, `userId`, `activeOrgId: null`, the token hash, `createdAt` / `updatedAt`, and `expiresAt` thirty days out (`SESSION_TTL_DAYS`). The raw token is not written. A dump of `sessions` cannot be replayed as a login.
- The function returns `{ token, expiresAt }`. `login` returns `{ user, token }` to the action. The action discards `user`.

`loginAction` then calls `resolveSession(token)`, which hashes the token again and loads the row through `findSessionByTokenHash`. That returns a `SessionPrincipal`: `userId`, `email`, `activeOrgId` (null on a fresh login), and `expiresAt`. There is no session id and no token on that type. If the lookup misses, the action throws `UnauthorizedActionError`.

`setSessionCookie` in `src/lib/session.ts` is the only writer of the cookie jar. It sets `taskflow_session` (`SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` in `src/schemas/session.ts`) to the raw token, `httpOnly`, `sameSite: "lax"`, `secure` in production, `path: "/"`, expiring at `principal.expiresAt`.

The action result sent back to the form is `{ ok: true, data: principal }`. So the browser’s JavaScript sees the user id, email, active org (null), and expiry. The password stays in `users.password_hash`. The token hash stays in `sessions.token_hash`. The raw token exists only inside the `Set-Cookie` header.

`LoginForm`’s effect then calls `router.push(next)`.
